_README: EXAMPLE ONLY. The real file lives in YOUR DATA OVERLAY, never in the engine
repo: <data-root>/admin/executives.json (normally ../.heading-os-data/admin/).
It is classified `private` in config/routing-map.yaml and must stay that way:
it carries real names, GitHub handles and repository names.
WHAT IT IS: the HEADING OS FLEET ROSTER. It answers exactly one question:
who is provisioned as a HEADING OS user. Nothing else belongs in it.
You only need this file if you run HEADING OS for more than one person. A
single-operator install has no fleet, the loader returns an empty roster,
and that is not an error.
ITS SIBLING: <data-root>/config/exec-registry.json is a DIFFERENT file
answering a DIFFERENT question: who is an executive in your ORGANISATION
(title, email, business role). See scripts/exec-registry.example.json.
Keep them apart. Someone can be one and not the other: an executive who
does not use HEADING OS, or an assistant who uses it and is not an
executive. Merging the two forces one row to carry two independent
lifecycles, and the copied fact goes stale. Join them with
scripts.utils.workspace.load_fleet(), which labels which file each fact
came from.
SINGLE WRITER: admin/provision/registry.py. Edit by hand only to change a
status.

_schema.slug: kebab-case identifier. The join key with exec-registry.json, and the suffix of their data repo.
_schema.name: Display name.
_schema.role: Short role token used by the engine (exec, cso, cfo, coo, ...).
_schema.github_user: Their GitHub username. They are added as a collaborator on their own data repo.
_schema.data_repo: Name of their private data overlay repo, by convention heading-os-data-{slug}.
_schema.status: See the vocabulary below. ONLY 'active' counts as fleet membership for aggregation and sync.

_status_vocabulary.provisioning: Setup is in flight. Nothing is guaranteed to exist yet.
_status_vocabulary.provisioned: Setup finished end to end, but the person has not started using it. Their repo holds only the setup commits.
_status_vocabulary.active: In use. This is the only status that makes them part of the fleet: aggregation, sync and fleet health all filter on it.
_status_vocabulary.offboarded: They have left. Access removed, repo archived.
_status_vocabulary.revoked: Access pulled in an emergency, ahead of a full offboard.
